page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 8369B processors operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. Managed via the KVM hypervisor, the instance allocates 8 dedicated virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. Hardware specifications include 16.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It incorporates hardware vector acceleration including AVX-512F and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside cryptographic instruction sets such as AES and SHA_NI. Network connectivity is delivered with a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. The instance does not include local NVMe storage or discrete GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations reveal middle-tier CPU execution performance paired with distinct memory bandwidth constraints. Synthetic CPU tests across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark consistently output scores within average performance brackets, backed by an L3 cache of 48 MB. However, memory subsystem performance degrades significantly during uncached memory access. Large-block uncached read speeds of 21.36 GB/sec and write speeds of 23.88 GB/sec place the instance in lower percentiles for throughput. This memory bottleneck extends to larger model inference, where text generation speed drops significantly on 7B parameter models despite baseline single-core performance.

Qualitative cost efficiency for the ecs.c7.2xlarge relies on workloads prioritizing dedicated CPU processing density over high-throughput RAM access or local disk I/O. The instance delivers steady performance for Redis key-value caching, static web traffic handling, software compilation, and microservice workloads. It is less suited for memory-bound data analysis, heavy local matrix computations, or large language model inference due to memory bandwidth constraints and reliance on remote network storage.
